Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
with a minimal level of CapEx within the business expected moving forward. Just turn now to operational update. We had a strong start to FY26, as outlined. The Tasman integration is on track, and the network synergies are approximately 50% complete. We expect those to be completed towards the end of June this financial year. In terms of the businesses themselves, we had strong performance across all the divisions. We're seeing good organic revenue growth, and strong new sales contracts signed of 5.4. Also a number of key wins with a range of corporate and government clients, plus a strong pipeline in all divisions. Global has got circa 450,000 MRR in the pipeline.
Convert that to annual recurring revenue, you just multiply that by 12, so that's around the AUD 5 million of annual recurring revenue in the pipeline. Our domestic network and cloud investments, in line with the TasmaNet acquisition and the consolidation of our network, we're continuing to upgrade and synergize our Australian mainline network, and more, I'll show you a little bit more on that in a moment. We have incurred some one-off CapEx to facilitate that upgrade. We bought some newer equipment, some more higher capacity equipment. We believe that it'll be around the circa AUD 500,000 to be incurred within FY 26.
That greater capacity core network, if you like, enables us to sell higher speed services, 1 gig type services, but also to replace what we effectively have with 3 networks. We're also upgrading our private cloud instances as well. That key rationalization project that I alluded to, expected to deliver circa or up to AUD 2 million per annum in savings. New sales performance, just giving a little bit more granularity on that in this update. If we look at FY24, FY25, you can see the first half figures coming in at, you know, approximately half the FY25, but a really good balance of sales across the various divisions. These are new sales contracts signed, and these are expressed in terms of annual recurring revenue.
Typically, we'd sign a total contract value with a customer. Depending upon the division that is, that could be, you know, 6 months, 12 months, 2 years, 3 years in terms of the TCV. Really good to see that balance across the business. We did secure a major contract and expansion of connectivity with a key customer in TasmaNet, a major global food producer. Really happy with that contract. Global itself saw very strong growth with, you know, 500+ new orders to about circa 80 international and domestic customers within the period, typically MNCs, multinational corporates, business-type customers. In late November 2025, we secured a major contract with a leading foreign government, valued at circa $70,000 of monthly recurring revenue. Really happy with that.
As at February 2025, Global had about AUD 2 million in annual recurring revenue to be provisioned, with a further AUD 72,000 in MRR at the contracting stage. AUD 2 million in ARR that has already been contracted but isn't on our books yet. In other words, we're not billing for that. Then another AUD 72,000 in MRR. You could just convert that to ARR multiplied by 12. You know, at the contracting stage, that, in other words, we've got an indication that we've won those deals and we're just finalizing the contracting. Separate to that, open opportunities in the Global pipeline of circa AUD 5 million. We're seeing a lot of great opportunities in Global across our footprint. Just on some of those key projects, we signed a global SaaS provider.
We announced that to the market in September 2024. 100% of those countries and services have been delivered at 31 December, all 11 jurisdictions. That service is up and fully billing or tolling, as we call it. We also signed a large global technology company for a significant service. We announced that to the market in November 2024. We have delivered technically on that service. We're just going through final testing, and there's been some delays, not with us, but with some other parties in relation to that. We're hopeful that we'll get that up and tolling around the Q3 period, FY26. At this stage, we're only billing around about the 5% level for that particular customer, a major Australian global food producer. I mentioned that one before.
We've delivered around 40% of that project, and that's been rolled out over the next few months, and then that leading foreign government in the Asia Pacific. We've delivered 100% of the services as at 31 December. That particular service is up and tolling at circa AUD 70,000 a month. Just on our global network, we're just, we keen to give the market a bit of an update on what's happening there. We tend to only go into a market, a new market, when we have customer demand. We don't go into the market for no other reason. We've continued to expand that network. Now the Asia Pacific coverage is pretty well at a point where we have 95% coverage.
We made a decision circa 5 years ago to get licenses in key markets because we could see that the regulators were making it difficult for some resellers out there. You can see our license markets over on the left there. It is our view that we would be the most licensed provider across the market. As a result, we're servicing a lot of large global carriers, you know, significant carriers from around the world, who then want to provide the services to their multinational corporates. They want to make sure that the provider is fully compliant. So they're not gonna go to some of these resellers out there in the market who really don't have the wherewithal, the reputation, the coverage, or the licenses. Within the period, we obtained a license in Vietnam.
We understand that we're the first foreign company to obtain that license. We'll probably be making a bit more of announcement on that in the next couple of weeks. In addition to that, we have circa six European markets where we have licensed or registered to provide those services there, as Europe is also tightening up. Keep in mind, we're providing local voice services with local telephone numbers in markets, and the regulators generally wanna make sure that you're compliant in that particular area. That's Europe and rest of world where we're expanding. We have a number of key markets that we're currently expanding into, that are on foot currently.
Our key differentiation is the fact that we do have these local telco licenses in key markets, and hence, we have the ability to provide compliant voice services and satisfy the requirements of some of the world's biggest companies. Separately from that footprint expansion, we're looking at expanding our go-to-market channels, including adding some new carrier partners over the next six to twelve months. In terms of the TasmaNet transition update, you can see there that we've been very successful in terms of getting customers and suppliers across. That's all been done. Now we're working on the integration and rationalization of that network and cloud platform, and we're circa 40, 50% done on that. We estimate that the TasmaNet related revenues within the period, the first half, was circa AUD 9 million. Really happy with that result.
That's made up of the customers and revenue that came across, but we also been able to grow that base and win some additional key contracts. We mentioned the global food producer. We also won some really good business in regional New South Wales with some key corporates and also with a government organization. This slide, which we've shown you before, really outlines what we're doing with that rationalization and consolidation process, where we're bringing together a number of o
ur core networks and our cloud platform. In doing this, we're also upgrading the technology, to give us a state-of-the-art network and cloud environment.
We'll end up with a cloud environment, private cloud environment in Brisbane, in Sydney, and in Tasmania, in Hobart, and key points of presence in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Hobart as well. I'll just turn now to strategy and outlook. In terms of strategy and outlook, continued focus on corporate mid-market government sectors domestically, and then, as I mentioned before, within the Asia Pacific and beyond, servicing multinational corporates. Most of our businesses or most of our customers, and users on our global network, at the end of the day, are multinational corporates, whether they're coming in directly or indirectly. We do win some business directly. We've just brought a major Australian bank online in a particular country in the Asia Pacific.
We expect to see more of that over time as well, with Australian corporates saying, "Well, who can we deal with that can provide us these global voice services?" We want to continue to cross-sell and upsell to these key strategic accounts of ours. Financial outlook, we're looking at annualized revenue of AUD 75 million plus, once TasmaNet fully transitioned. As you can see, for the first half, we were already over the halfway mark for that, and we expect annualized EBITDA of AUD 9 to 10 million once that transition and rationalization process is finished. We want to continue to grow our operating and free cash flow a little bit within this period of additional costs that were incurred and a working capital increase.
As moving forward, we expect that to go back to that growth period that we had before, and continue to deliver good shareholder returns. In terms of the final figure for this year, I think as we get closer towards the end of the year, we can give the market a bit more of an update there. Growth opportunities, I think I've covered a lot of those. We're seeing some really good organic growth opportunities and or inorganic in the market. We still have some active M&A discussions ongoing, but the last six months, the key focus has been on, you know, that rationalization process and getting the TasmaNet business fully integrated and pulling out those costs, those synergy costs, that we saw. We're working on that. Expect to finish that around the June period.
At this stage, I'm gonna hand back to Daniel, and very happy to take any questions from yourselves.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Thank you, Peter. We have a number of questions online, I'll read out the first question. Peter, can you clarify whether the AUD 9 to 10 million EBITDA exit run rate guidance includes the AUD 2 million benefit from the rationalization project to be completed in Q4?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Yes, that is correct. One thing I would state is we're already starting to see some of those benefits come through. You can see there that, and we mentioned in the deck that we're around the 40% mark. We've already actually done quite a lot of that project, and we expect to finish the project by around about, you know, the June month or thereabouts. Yes, that 9 to 10 pretty well includes that rationalization project.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Second question? After signing Vodafone, the Vodafone Global Partnership mid-2022, global segment revenue grew from AUD 10.2 million to AUD 15.3 million from FY22 to calendar year 2025. How much of that revenue delta is from Vodafone, and how much further growth does this partnership provide the group?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Yeah, look, the Vodafone partnership has been very instrumental for us. You know, the fact that we could deliver the services that we delivered to them, a number of key unified communications products globally for them. Our product set with Vodafone is pretty well steady now, but we are adding additional countries over time for them. We see some further growth opportunities there. Look, I'm not at liberty to say what the total revenue is with Vodafone, but it is very decent. They would be one of our top global customers, but we do expect that to continue to grow over time.
In addition to Vodafone, we would have a number of other key partners similar to Vodafone that we've been able to bring on as well, that are, you know, almost as significant as Vodafone as well, and we would expect that strategy to be replicated with additional partners over time. I think the Vodafone thing firstly gave us a lot of credibility in the market. We were able to deliver really well for Vodafone. Vodafone are very happy with our performance and the types of services that we deliver for them. We took them to Operator Connect, for those who are aware of that marketplace. All in all, a very, very positive relationship with good momentum and continuing to grow and build over time.
We also deliver quite a lot of services into Europe, you know, in conjunction with Vodafone, not just in the Asia-Pacific region, so in other parts of the world. As we expand our market reach into other markets, you know, other parts of the world, whether that be Europe, Asia-Pacific, I don't want to name the specific parts of the world, but we've got some active expansions underway currently. We would expect to see both Vodafone and a number of other carriers take those services from us. All in all, a really positive relationship, which is growing. I think you can assume that the revenue that we're getting from Vodafone is in the millions. It's not just them that's a key customer for us now.
Just on, Daniel, if I just extend the question a little bit wider, you know, yes, I think you can see that the revenue's gone from circa AUD 10 million. I think if you, the person who asked that question is indicated, yes, circa AUD 15 million. I think if you look at our gross revenue of AUD 7.9, which is selling also to our domestic businesses who onsell to their customers, we're more like about AUD 16 million with our work in progress, as we call it, our WIP contract signed. You can see that that's probably going more like AUD 18, 19 million. We probably see that global business, we, you know, we look at that as around a AUD 20 million turnover business today.
Yes, we haven't delivered that yet, but that's what we're seeing, that is with the customers in the pipeline, et cetera. You know, we've largely, haven't got there yet, but largely doubled the revenue in that business in the last two or three years, so really happy with the performance within that business.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
We have a question here. This week, Aussie Broadband acquired Nextgen at 6.3x EBITDA. Considering the company, i.e., Comms Group, is trading on 4x, has the board considered a strategic review to achieve a sale outcome like Nextgen?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Look, the board, myself and the board, we're always looking at ways to maximize value for shareholders. You know, we have various people approach us over time. I think you can be rest assured that the board, you know, considers all strategic options, you know, on a regular basis. We do meet to discuss these things regularly. I can't go into any specifics, but, you know, it is something that we're very mindful of as well.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Regarding the secured managed IP solution segment, do you see or expect any positive or negative impact as customers accelerate AI capability adoption, modernizing their IT capabilities in-house? Just follow on from that, is your pricing seat-based and potentially subject to the risk of customers reducing their IT team headcounts, replacing with AI capabilities?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Look, we tend to target mid-market within that business, so corporate mid-market. A little bit bigger than more, bigger than the SME, but I think in general, the SME in the mid-market, the biggest issue that they've had is not just, you know, what product do I get? Do I get the latest virus checker, is that gonna work? Can I do AI or whatever? I think it's making sure that they're covering all bases. Cybersecurity is a really big issue. Security risks are a really big issue, but the fact that they're continuing to move to the cloud. What we're finding is that the mid-market corporates are more and more interested in our services, not less interested. We don't see that AI is going to come along and solve everything for them.
If anything, it's going to create more and more security risks for them. As people tend to run things like ChatGPT, and they start to use more AI within their business, they're going to need a very robust and secure IT environment. We're finding that this is creating great opportunities for us. Now, from our perspective, we're looking to use AI and some of the core operational systems within our secure managed IT solutions business to improve our service delivery for our customers. Just as businesses are looking at what they can do with AI and other advanced technologies, we ourselves are starting to look at how we're already implementing how we can deliver a better service for our customers. That core essence of, I'm a mid-market corporate, small business, mid-market corporate, how do I make sure that I'm
secure?
Is the, is a key thematic for us within the growth that we're seeing in that market. They can't just rely on their IT teams, and some of them actually want to run relatively small IT teams, so they need a provider who can help them with that. That's where, you know, our security essentials product is really good. You know, we deliver a managed security solution, not just, I'll get the latest virus checker, because a lot of businesses don't know whether that's going to work or not, and they don't know what product to buy anyhow. It's a holistic approach across their whole environment. There is a, you know, a strong thematic. They're using, moving to more and more cloud applications.
We are interestingly seeing private cloud raise its head again, and we're seeing a lot of businesses want to put quite a lot of information into private cloud. We're a big private cloud provider, so that's important, an important thing as well. You know, if anything, we're seeing good growth within that business, and you would have seen our margins, continue to be very healthy as well.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Next question, would you consider selling the global segment?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Look, whether we would sell or not sell, it's not something we could go into at this stage. I mean, obviously, you know, if someone came along and made us a good offer, we, it's something we might consider, but we do think that that is a really good business. It's got some unique characteristics. It's taking us quite a long period to get to where we are. You can't easily get licenses, particularly in that region, we've developed a really strong sense of, you know, as a great provider to a number of big carriers globally. It's not just that we're in those markets, we're very personalized service, we run 24 by 7. They know if there's an issue, we're going to fix it, et cetera, et cetera.
We deal with all of these carriers across the region, in the current time zone. If you're a US or European carrier, you can't do that. The people you need to speak to don't work at nighttime in Asia. They work during the day, so we can tap into them. There's lots of aspects about global that are really positive, but you know, ultimately, we're here to maximize value for shareholders, so we would consider things as they come along.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
What percentage of the AUD 450,000 MRR in the global pipeline would you expect to convert based on historical pipeline conversion rates?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Yes. Of that figure, there's two aspects. There's the amount that's already contracted and to be provisioned. We tend to provision services very quickly. That government deal that we provisioned, we had that up and running within 2 to 4 weeks into a key Asian country. It's a significant, chunky deal. There's the aspect of the deals that are already there in work in progress, as we call it. We would expect those to be delivered pretty rapidly. We have that one large deal that's, you know, circa maybe AUD 150 a month or thereabout, maybe a little bit more. We're hoping that that can be delivered very shortly.
The deals within the, that have contracted but not ready to be, you know, signed off, if you like, at this point, are probably going to take within the next six months to be delivered. I would say three to six months.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
On inorganic opportunities, is there a particular segment within the business that could benefit most from accelerated scale or increased capabilities?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Yes. Look, we do like the, you know, secure managed IT solutions, so any opportunities there would be good. We have quite good scale there, but we'd like to increase the capabilities there. That would, or the size of that business. Keep in mind, we're very much a managed service provider with contracts and recurring revenue, so we really like that business. We, yeah, we would look for other kind of business telco opportunities as well. We can get scale from that also. Global, at this stage, global, we, you know, if the right type of thing came along, we'd say, wow, that'd be a great business to buy, but we're a little bit more cautious, particularly in the Asia Pacific region.
I think at this stage, LMNA mainly focused around domestic, but within those, both those telco services and managed IT services area.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Do contracts typically include CPI-linked reviews each year?
Peter McGrath
CEO and Managing Director, Comms Group Ltd
Depends on the type of contract. Some contracts do, but in gener
al, it's not something that we've put a lot of that in, but, you know, we have been considering how we could do that moving forward. you know, a lot of other industries do that today, and we probably need to learn something from that. telco, in general, has been a little bit tardy with some of that in the past, but it is something that we've considered looking at and doing. As I think things like the NBN and the like, the pricing there tends to stabilize. It's probably an area that we could explore at some point, but at this stage, we don't have a lot of CPI-linked price increases in our contracts.
Daniel Ireland
Investor Relations, Comms Group Ltd
Okay. That's all the questions that we have. I'd like to thank Peter and Matthew for the presentation today, and thank you for attending.
Thank you, everyone, for attending.
